vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
A **web developer or technical SEO consultant** can check the site and make the changes. Ask for an **AI crawler-accessibility audit and implementation**, not just an “AI SEO” package.

They should check:
- `robots.txt` and page-level `noindex` or bot directives
- CDN, firewall, or hosting rules that may return blocks or captchas to bots
- Whether important pages are readable without heavy JavaScript or a login
- Access for the specific bots you want to allow—for example, search/discovery bots such as **OAI-SearchBot** and **PerplexityBot**. Some bots, such as **GPTBot**, relate to model training; you may want a different policy for them.

For a specialist option, Elementive advertises an AI crawlability and visibility audit that tests bots and identifies issues such as firewall blocks: [Elementive AI Crawlability & Visibility Audit](https://www.elementive.com/ai-crawlability-visibility-audit/). You can also ask your current web developer or SEO agency to do the same work.

Before hiring, confirm they’ll **show you the findings, get your approval on which bots to allow, make the changes, and retest**. Don’t allow every crawler automatically—some settings govern training use, not whether your business appears in AI search. And access alone can’t guarantee that an assistant will mention your business.
